concepts.def: Adds a reward to repeat behaviour
Adds a cost to stop behaviour

walkthroughs.body_html:
B.F. Skinner put rats in a box with a lever.

Press lever → food drops in. Rats soon pressed it lots.

That's positive reinforcement at work. 🐀

• Positive reinforcement — add nice (sticker).
  • Negative reinforcement — remove nasty (no homework if good).
  • Positive punishment — add nasty (detention).
  • Negative punishment — remove nice (phone away).

Operant conditioning is everywhere:

  • House points at school.
  • Pocket money for chores.
  • Game level-ups.
  • Loyalty stamps at cafés.

Rewards usually beat punishments. ⭐
